newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks open down in listless pre-Christmas trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks open down in listless pre-Christmas trade.

text.p: Australian shares opened slightly weaker on light volume with many investors absent from the market ahead of the Christmas break on Wednesday and Thursday.
At 10.20 a.m. (1120 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.5 points weaker at 2,375.0.
The December share price index was down three points at 2,383 and at an eight point premium to the underlying index.
Early activity was dominated by Westpac Banking Corp whose shares went ex-dividend, paying a final dividend of 17 cents a share.
"There was a little bit of selling in the resources sector early but this seems to be drying up along with business in general," a dealer from a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said most brokers were running with less than half staff and with the market closing three hours early at 1.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), trading activity was likely to remain very light.

Shares in regional banks Advance and St George continued to travel in opposing directions with Advance firmer and St George weaker after Advance shareholders approved a scheme to merge with St George on Monday.
At 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), St George shares were 11 cents weaker at A$7.77 (US$6.22) while Advance shares were six cents higher at A$6.96.
